summary: Discovery with SaltBay (mid-market bank) to evaluate Redwood Dedicated for production LLM inference. Key constraints: EU data residency, SOC2/KMS, P95 latency target ~250ms for small-chat + batch embedding workloads, expected seasonal bursts during month-end with peak qps ~450. Discussed isolation (VPC + reserved GPUs), burst strategy (burst pool + autoscale), and pilot timeline (Q3 pilot). Agreed next steps: pricing, security pack, and technical deep dive + benchmark plan.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-02 14:00 PDT | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Michael (CTO SaltBay), Priya (Head of ML), Laura (Security), Owen (Infra), Sara (Product)

00:00 - Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood, and with me is Daniel, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 - Michael: Good, thanks. Busy month but excited to talk through this.
00:10 - Aisha: Great. Quick agenda: we want to understand your workload, constraints, and talk through Dedicated reserved GPU options, burst strategy, and next steps for a pilot. Does that sound right?
00:18 - Priya: Yep that works. We'll probably talk a lot about latency and data residency.
00:22 - Daniel: Cool. Could you give us a quick overview of the models and traffic profile? Rough numbers are fine.
00:28 - Priya: Sure. We run two main inference flows: a chat assistant for consumer banking (short contexts, 100-300 tokens) and an embeddings pipeline for fraud detection/reranking (batch 128-512 items). The chat is most latency-sensitive. Average qps is ~120 but peaks up to ~450 during month-end and marketing pushes. We expect 10x growth over 12 months.
00:44 - Owen: Infra is mostly AWS, EKS, some on-prem for legacy systems. We need EU data residency for a subset of traffic and can't send certain PII to third-party hosted services without controls.
00:55 - Daniel: Thanks. For the chat P95 target what are you aiming for?
01:00 - Priya: Ideally P95 < 250ms for the chat path. Embeddings can be higher, up to 2s is okay.
01:07 - Aisha: Good, that helps. A lot to unpack. On the Dedicated side we offer reserved GPU pools that are isolated to your tenancy, plus burst capacity handles spikes. You can pin models and we support KMS for key management and audit logs.
01:20 - Laura: On KMS, we need to integrate with our AWS KMS and ensure keys never leave our account. Is that supported?
01:26 - Daniel: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private and Dedicated VPC setups. For Hosted we do bring-your-own-key in some configurations, but Dedicated gives tighter controls.
01:36 - Laura: And SOC 2?
01:38 - Aisha: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts; we'll share the security pack. We also support SAML SSO and RBAC for role separation.
01:46 - Michael: Great. Cost is obviously a factor. We're trying to balance latency with cost; can you summarize tradeoffs?
01:53 - Daniel: Sure. Low-latency single-token generation benefits from smaller batch sizes and more reserved capacity; that increases cost. For embeddings batch processing, you get better utilization with batching and quantized models — lower per-unit cost. Dedicated reserved GPUs reduce variability and are more cost-predictable vs hosted burst pricing.
02:09 - Sara: For burst, do you rely on auto-scaling GPUs or a shared burst pool? We have spiky windows and don't want throttling.
02:16 - Daniel: We have both. You can configure reserved pools for baseline throughput, plus a burst pool that autos-scales within your dedicated region/account. There are policies for graceful degradation — e.g., route lower-priority traffic to cheaper quantized variants or to Hosted fallback in cross-account scenarios.
02:30 - Priya: Are rollouts and canaries supported? We do a lot of model A/B testing.
02:34 - Aisha: Yes, the Console supports canary rollouts and A/B. You can pin percentages by route and monitor per-model latency/cost traces.
02:40 - Owen: On-network topology — we need VPC peering and strict egress rules. Does Dedicated support customer VPC?
02:46 - Daniel: Dedicated can be deployed in your VPC (Private deployment) or as a VPC-connected dedicated pool depending on the setup. For full isolation we recommend Private deployment (on-prem or in-customer VPC with control plane options).
02:58 - Michael: Hmm, given compliance our preference is a Dedicated in our EU VPC. We don't want tokens leaving the region.
03:05 - Aisha: That's a common ask. We can scope a Dedicated EU cluster with reserved GPUs and KMS integration.
03:09 - Laura: One more question on logging and audit — do you provide per-request logs and token-level tracing?
03:14 - Daniel: We provide per-request traces, cost and latency breakdowns; token-level logging is available with opt-in and controlled retention. We can also forward logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
03:24 - Priya: For benchmarks: what's the typical throughput for a gpus type — are we talking A100, H100, or L2s?
03:30 - Daniel: We support multiple GPU types. For inference we often recommend H100 or A100 for high-throughput low-latency models. We can quantify expected qps per GPU for your model once we have the model binary and seq-length distribution. We'll run a micro-benchmark in the pilot.
03:44 - Priya: We'll need to confirm whether we'll serve open models or our fine-tuned variant — for cost we might do a quantized 4-bit variant in production. Any issues there?
03:52 - Daniel: 4-bit quantization is supported; runtime picks optimal kernels. There are sometimes quality tradeoffs but we can recommend quantization profiles that preserve quality.
04:01 - Michael: Timeline: we want a pilot in Q3, ideally in September, to validate P95 latency and cost baseline. Is that feasible?
04:07 - Aisha: Yes, that's doable. Typical path: sign an NDA/Security questionnaire, share workload artifacts, run a 2-4 week pilot, then SOW for Dedicated reserved capacity.
04:16 - Laura: On the legal side we'll need data processing addendum and evidence of controls.
04:20 - Aisha: We'll send the DPA and security pack.
04:23 - Sara: For success criteria, Priya and I discussed: P95 chat <250ms, embeddings throughput >= X per GPU, and cost-per-1M tokens under target. We'll formalize in pilot doc.
04:34 - Priya: Also need to run regression checks against current models, we can't have quality regressions when quantizing.
04:39 - Daniel: We support eval harnesses and can run prompt-based regressions with your test sets during the pilot.
04:45 - Michael: Any gotchas with burst — like cold starts if we scale up GPUs?
04:49 - Daniel: There can be a cold-start latency when the autoscaler spins up extra nodes; we mitigate that with warm standby instances and pre-warming policies. Burst pools can be pre-warmed for predictable windows.
04:59 - Owen: How does billing for burst work vs reserved?
05:02 - Aisha: Reserved is a monthly committed invoice; burst is metered usage on top with defined price tiers. We'll include example math in the pricing doc for your traffic profile.
05:12 - Priya: For monitoring, what telemetry will you need from us to size properly?
05:16 - Daniel: Ideally: request size distribution, seq-length distribution, sample logs, and peak qps by time window. We'll also request a small model binary or an ONNX/torchscript snapshot for microbenchmarks.
05:28 - Michael: Ok we'll gather that.
05:31 - Aisha: Next steps recap: We'll send pricing + Dedicated SKUs, security pack (SOC2/ISO/DPA/KMS notes), and propose a technical deep dive next week to plan benchmarks. You (Priya/Owen) will share workload traces and model artifacts.
05:44 - Priya: Sounds good. Any open concerns?
05:47 - Laura: One last on retention — we want logs to be retained for 1 year and archived. Is that configurable?
05:52 - Daniel: Yes, retention is configurable per-tenant; we can forward to your S3/Cloud storage for long term.
05:59 - Michael: Thanks everyone, this was useful. Look forward to the pricing doc.
06:03 - Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up on the action items.

(Transcript notes: automated speech recognition; occasional mis-attribution and minor word errors. Some technical terms transcribed phonetically or with alternate acronyms.)
